hypothesis: If the claim holds, essentially no native non-volant, non-marine mammals will occur on islands more than about 483 km (300 miles) from a continent or large continental island.
pass_criterion: Of the islands >100 km2 lying more than 483 km from the nearest continent or large continental island, at most 2 have a native terrestrial non-volant mammal in IUCN range data, excluding species introduced by humans.
fail_criterion: More than 5 such islands have a native terrestrial mammal, for example Galapagos rice rats or Hawaiian or Philippine endemic rodents.
interpretation: 'Terrestrial mammal' means non-flying, non-marine mammals. The 300-mile threshold converts to 483 km. 'Great continental island' means islands such as Borneo or Great Britain. Distances must be computed from a landmass shapefile. Bats and pinnipeds are excluded.

dataset.name: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species - Terrestrial Mammals spatial data and range maps
dataset.why_it_fits: Fields used: species range polygons, presence code (extant, native origin) and taxonomic order. Spatial overlay with island polygons gives native mammals per island.
